Bring the `{dir}/` folder back to how it was at version `{version}` ({subject}). History stays as it is: this is a new change, handed in for review.

- [ ] In your worktree: `git restore --source={commit} --staged --worktree -- {dir}` — files added since go too
- [ ] If there is a UI map, check its pictures still match the code, and shoot them again where they don't
- [ ] Say what came back (tokens · logo · UI map · guidelines) and hand it in for review

routine.design_review.prompt:
Weekly design review — bring it to me once a week, in one message I can react to quickly.
1. What’s out of line: on each project with a design folder, run `equipe design flows check` and look at the UI map itself beside tokens.json and guidelines.md — inconsistencies, missing states, stale pictures, drift from the design system. Pick at most three, each with its picture and where it is (Flow › Screen › State).
2. One proposal to refine, shown on real screens: what is there now beside your option, put to me with `ask_decision` as a visual question I answer in one click. Run `equipe design critique` on its pictures first, and attach what it found, in short.
3. Two or three references worth a look, from design/references/ first: each with its link and what to take from it.
Read my taste before you choose, and follow it — the squad’s `design taste notes` and `design taste` in its memory, the project’s design/taste.md and design/decisions/. Head the message “Weekly design review”, the three parts in this order. Change nothing — files, tokens or tickets — until I’ve chosen.
routine.design_review.setup: The weekly design review starts once the design setup is done. The setup of {design} is at step {n} of five, {step}. Please carry on with it, and put what’s mine to decide to me on a card. If you’re already on it, just tell me in a line where it stands.
routine.design_review.title: Design review
routine.retro.prompt:
Weekly retro. Below, under [Retro facts · …], equipe has gathered this week's facts from the squad's journal: write from them and invent nothing — where they don't say, say so.
Bring it to me in one message headed “Weekly retro”, in this order:
1. Shipped: the tickets that landed on main, each as its T- number and title.
2. Stuck and why: stuck turns, failed tickets, work sent back, missed ETAs and the approvals members waited on me for — each with its cause, as far as the facts show.
3. Time by member: turns, time and usage per member and per ticket, and where the friction was, by member or role.
If a project has briefs (in the squad's folder, docs/<project>/briefs/), set what each expected beside what happened.
End with at most three lessons and at most three changes for next week. Put the changes to me in one `ask_decision`, one question per change, so each takes one click: the change as the first option, recommended, and “Not this week” as the last option. Give each question its `lesson`: the lesson behind it, in one line. equipe keeps the lessons of the changes I take in the squad's memory under "lessons", with the date; the rest are let go — don't remember them yourself.
Change nothing yourself — no setting, no routine: propose instead (a proposed ticket, `propose_routine`), and only my click turns anything on.

routine.weekly_check_in.prompt:
Weekly check-in.
1. Last week in short: what was finished, what moved, what got stuck.
2. Look at the metrics and the feedback we have — analytics, reviews, issues, messages — and say what changed.
3. Propose the next 1–3 pieces of work toward the goal, each as a proposed ticket.
4. Gather what I need to decide into one card.
routine.weekly_check_in.title: Weekly check-in
card.signal_on: Turn on the signal {name} for {project}: every {every}, run `{command}` — expect {expect}
card.signal_change: Change the signal {name} of {project}: every {every}, run `{command}` — expect {expect}
routine.weekly_security.title: Weekly security check
routine.weekly_security.prompt:
Weekly security check. Give the review to the security member as a ticket.
1. Start with the code and the dependencies that changed since the last check.
2. Check known vulnerabilities, leaked secrets, settings exposed to the outside, and this machine's basic security settings.
3. List what you find by severity and propose the fixes as tickets for the engineers. Tell me at once about anything severe.
4. Keep the report in the squad's folder under security/, by date.
routine.weekly_marketing.title: Weekly marketing check
routine.weekly_marketing.prompt:
Weekly marketing check. Give it to the marketing member.
1. Look at last week's content and numbers (visits, sign-ups, responses) and tell me what worked.
2. Propose 1–3 pieces of content or experiments for this week, with drafts.
3. Anything public stays a draft until I say yes to it.
4. Keep the results in the squad's folder under marketing/, by date.

secrets.grant.question: Let {member} use the key “{name}” ({service}) on {project}?
secrets.grant.here_desc: You're asked once for each project.
secrets.grant.any_desc: You won't be asked again for this key.
secrets.grant.no_desc: The member goes on without it.
secrets.replace.question: {member} wants to replace the key “{name}” ({service}), saved by {by}, with a new value. Replace it?
secrets.replace.yes_desc: The new value takes the old one's place everywhere it is used.
design_session.question: A short design session on {screen} first?
design_session.kickoff: Let's work on {page} together, in short rounds.
design_session.no_designer: There's no designer on the team for a design session yet. Ask the PM to bring one in.
design_session.no_page: Name the page or screen the design session is on.
design_session.use_intro: Picked in a design session with "Use this": build this prototype in the product.
deploy.yours_live_on: What you asked for is live on {host}:
deploy.yours_live: What you asked for is live in {project}:
deploy.yours_on_main: What you asked for is on main in {project}:
autonomy.floor: {kind} always asks you — no policy changes that.
autonomy.used: ✓ {name} went ahead under your standing allowance ({scope}): {action}
autonomy.policy_used: ✓ {name} went ahead under the squad's policy for live data: {action}
autonomy.picked: {name} picked «{picked}»{why} — you didn't answer within the window. You can change it.
control.autonomy_window: Decide-and-tell choices wait {minutes} min for you
news.growth_run: Growth run: {count} numbers read; the PM turns them into cards for you.
news.growth_nothing: Growth run: no numbers to work from ({why}).
news.growth_budget: Growth run: not handed to the PM — the loop's weekly token budget is spent.
news.growth_live: G-{id} “{title}” is live with T-{ticket}: measured again in 7 and 14 days.
news.growth_worked: G-{id} “{title}”, {days} days live: it worked — {after} beside {before} before ({pct}).
news.growth_no_change: G-{id} “{title}”, {days} days live: no change — {after} beside {before} before ({pct}).
news.growth_worse: G-{id} “{title}”, {days} days live: worse — {after} beside {before} before ({pct}).
news.growth_unmeasured: G-{id} “{title}”, {days} days live: it couldn't be measured again.
sprint.start_picked: Start with the items I tick below
sprint.q_items: Which items? Ticking any starts those instead of the recommended ones.
sprint.started_on_own: Already started on its own (your autonomy setting): cancel its ticket to stop it.
sprint.outside: Whatever it publishes, posts, emails or spends waits for your yes.
sprint.q_market: Will people pay for this product?
sprint.market_internal: No, an internal tool or just for me
news.sprint_proposed: Sprint S-{id} proposed with {count} items: start it with one tap on its card.
news.sprint_started: Sprint S-{id} started with {count} items; its review is on {end}.
news.sprint_auto_started: Sprint S-{id}: started on their own under your autonomy setting: {items}.
news.sprint_review: Sprint S-{id} has ended: the PM writes its retro and proposes the next one.
news.sprint_planning: The product is live: the PM plans its first sprint.
news.sprint_closed_quiet: Sprint S-{id} was closed on its numbers alone: the PM didn't write its retro within a day.
news.sprint_live: H-{id} “{belief}” is live: judged in {days} days by the rule set before it shipped.
news.sprint_inconclusive: H-{id} “{belief}”: inconclusive — the numbers don't settle it.
news.sprint_no_events: H-{id} “{belief}” is live, but its events ({events}) aren't arriving: it can't be measured until that's fixed.
news.sprint_budget: Sprint S-{id} has used {pct}% of its budget ({spent} of {budget} tokens).
